mcqs.learning_point: Understand the cell as the basic unit of life
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements reflects a common misconception about cells?

options.A: All living organisms are composed of one or more cells.
options.B: Cells are the basic structural and functional units of life.
options.C: Viruses are considered living cells because they can reproduce on their own.
options.D: Each cell can carry out all the processes required for life.

mcqs.answer: Viruses are considered living cells because they can reproduce on their own.
mcqs.explanation: Viruses are not cells; they lack cellular machinery such as a nucleus, ribosomes, and membranes, and cannot carry out metabolism or reproduce independently. Therefore option C is a misconception. Options A, B and D correctly describe cells: all living organisms are made of cells, cells are the basic unit of structure and function, and each cell can perform life processes.

mcqs.learning_point: State the basic ideas of cell theory
mcqs.question: Which statement best summarizes the three fundamental ideas of the cell theory?

options.A: All living things are made of cells; cells are the basic unit of structure and function; all cells arise from pre‑existing cells.
options.B: Cells can arise spontaneously from non‑living matter; cells are the smallest unit of life; all organisms contain a nucleus.
options.C: Only plants are composed of cells; cells are the basic unit of life; cells can be created in the laboratory.
options.D: Cells are the basic unit of life; all cells contain mitochondria; cells can divide indefinitely.

mcqs.answer: All living things are made of cells; cells are the basic unit of structure and function; all cells arise from pre‑existing cells.
mcqs.explanation: The cell theory consists of three main tenets: (1) all living organisms are composed of cells, (2) the cell is the basic structural and functional unit of life, and (3) all cells arise from pre‑existing cells. Option A states all three correctly. The other options contain false statements such as spontaneous generation, universal presence of mitochondria, or that only plants are cellular.

mcqs.question: Which of the following pairs correctly matches an organism with its classification and a characteristic that distinguishes it from the other type?

options.A: Amoeba – unicellular; its single cell performs all life functions independently.
options.B: Human – unicellular; its single cell performs all life functions independently.
options.C: Moss – multicellular; each of its cells can live independently outside the organism.
options.D: Bacteria – multicellular; its cells are highly specialized for different functions.

mcqs.answer: Amoeba – unicellular; its single cell performs all life functions independently.
mcqs.explanation: Amoeba is a classic example of a unicellular organism where one cell carries out all necessary functions. Humans are multicellular (option B is wrong), moss cells are specialized and cannot live independently (option C is wrong), and bacteria are unicellular, not multicellular with specialized cells (option D is wrong).

mcqs.question: Which organelle is primarily responsible for producing ATP, the energy currency of the cell, and why?

options.A: Nucleus – because it stores genetic material required for energy production.
options.B: Mitochondrion – because it carries out cellular respiration that generates ATP.
options.C: Ribosome – because it synthesizes proteins that store energy.
options.D: Golgi apparatus – because it packages and transports ATP molecules.

mcqs.answer: Mitochondrion – because it carries out cellular respiration that generates ATP.
mcqs.explanation: Mitochondria are the powerhouses of the cell; they perform oxidative phosphorylation during cellular respiration, producing ATP. The nucleus stores DNA, ribosomes synthesize proteins, and the Golgi apparatus modifies and packages proteins and lipids, but none directly generate ATP. Hence option B is correct.
